#1866. Barnsley FC 7 Aldershot Town 2: League One strugglers cruise into second round of FA Cup

Barnsley cruised into the second round of the FA Cup with an emphatic 7-2 win over Aldershot Town.

The fifth-tier Shots were ruthlessly dismantled by the third-tier Reds, who were clinical in front of a sparse Oakwell crowd.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Captain Cameron McGeehan stole the show with a hat-trick, while Vimal Yoganathan notched a brace and Reyes Cleary and Rylan Brownlie got in on the act.

Aldershot did give their travelling supporters something to celebrate late on when Annisuis Lewis struck twice, but they were merely consolations.

The game followed the natural order of cup ties when there is a division gap from the get-go, with the higher-ranked team enjoying the lion’s share of possession.

Ziyad Larkeche was the first to penetrate the Aldershot box, receiving a pass from Cleary on the overlap and fizzing a cross towards McGeehan. The cross was drilled at Barnsley’s captain rather than to him, therefore the midfielder could only bundle harmlessly wide.

Barnsley did have the ball in the back of the net early on, when McGeehan was sent through by Daniel Johnson and rolled it into the bottom corner, only for the offside flag to appear.

Aldershot were not dealing with an onslaught but there continued to be a steady flow of promising ventures forward by the hosts. A tidy swivel from Luca Connell in the middle of the park quickly shifted into attack and he picked out Tobi Adeyemo, who saw a tame shot held comfortably by Nick Hayes.

Aldershot’s goalkeeper, however, could not get to a McGeehan header sent towards the top corner after a peach of a delivery from Jubril Okedina.

Barnsley’s feet remained firmly pressed on the gas and the lead was doubled less than 10 minutes later. A Yoganathan cross was helped along from right to left by Adeyemo before it reached the feet of Cleary, who rifled home a rasping shot.

Aldershot had spent very little time in the ascendency but did muster a brief flicker after going 2-0 down. Hakeem Sandah jinked his way down the left before cutting in to pull the trigger, although his powerful drive was straight down the throat of Cieran Slicker.

Barnsley soon returned to the front foot and did not wait long before striking for a third time. Connell split the Shots defence with an incisive pass latched on to by Yoganathan, who kept his cool to slot past Hayes.

The visitors enjoyed their best spell late in the first half, knitting together some neat passes to emerge from their camped-in state and ask questions of the hosts. Dominic Odusanya stung the palms of Slicker and Sandah then forced the goalleeper to tip a dipping shot behind at full stretch.

However, the fourth goal of the game, on the stroke of half-time, was registered by Barnsley. Aldershot failed to deal with a Larkeche cross that made its way to Yoganathan, who steered home his second of the afternoon.

Makenzie Kirk replaced Tobi Adeyemo at the interval and was presented with a glorious opportunity less than five minutes into the second half. He found himself on the end of a slick move but Hayes produced an impressive save to thwart the on-loan Portsmouth man.

Aldershot struggled to clear their lines in the aftermath and Kirk should have had a second bite of the cherry, but McGeehan elected to shoot when a pass to the forward was a better option.

With Barnsley cruising, there was no urgent need for McGeehan to make amends, yet he did so regardless as he tapped home a fifth on the rebound after Kirk was denied.

Aldershot’s defensive door continued to creak open and Barnsley refused to relent in their pursuit of goals. McGeehan completed his hat-trick just five minutes after his second, striking low and hard after connecting with a Connell pass.

The visitors were well-backed and finally gave their supporters something to celebrate late on, when Lewis slipped in behind the Barnsley backline and tucked the ball away in the bottom corner.

Lewis found the target again in similar circumstances with four minutes of normal timne remaining, although it was not the final goal of the afternoon. Barnsley bit back immediately via substitute Brownlie, who tidly swept past Hayes to make it 7-2.

#1865. I watched Rangers beat St Mirren and spotted penalty controversy, growing Ibrox influence and big achievement

Rangers returned to winning ways on the road with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren in Paisley on Saturday night, extending their unbeaten domestic run to 12 matches in the process.

Derek McInnes' side had been held to draws in their previous two league fixtures away from home against Dundee and Hearts, but goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil ensured there would be no repeat disappointment at the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The result leaves the Ibrox side just one point behind Celtic at the top of the Scottish Premiership, although the league leaders have the opportunity to extend their advantage when they face Kilmarnock this afternoon.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold in Paisley for The Scotsman and picks out his three main takeaways from the game.

Rangers have now gone 12 matches without defeat in all competitions, a remarkable improvement given the uncertainty that followed McInnes' rocky start to life in Govan. Their success last night was thoroughly deserved but there remains considerable scope for improvement, particularly in the final third.

McInnes has warned that his team are not yet the finished article. There are still familiar frustrations he must continue to address. Rangers' inability to turn promising attacking situations into goals meant St Mirren remained in the contest for longer than they should have, while some questionable decision-making in the final third prevented the visitors from recording a more emphatic winning margin.

At the opposite end, though, Rangers continue to demonstrate the defensive resilience that has underpinned their domestic revival. Six clean sheets in 12 league outings represent a major achievement and provide McInnes with a solid base on which to build from. Olwethu Makhanya was fortunate to escape punishment for a couple of uncharacteristic errors on this occasion, but his defensive partner Emmanuel Fernandez produced a commanding performance to make up for it.

Rangers now have an international break to regroup before returning to Premiership action with a trip to Motherwell on November 21. McInnes will hope his players return refreshed, with the opportunity to build on their unbeaten sequence and address the attacking shortcomings that continue to prevent his side from reaching their full potential.

The game's major talking point came midway through the first-half when Rangers were awarded a penalty following a challenge by Samuel Ramos on James Penrice. The St Mirren man appeared to make minimal contact with the Rangers left-back inside the area, but referee Nick Walsh was quick in pointing to the spot.

Unsurprisingly, the decision did not go down well with the home support and Buddies boss Craig McLeish. They felt the contact from Ramos was insufficient to warrant a spot-kick, particularly given the nature of the challenge and Penrice's theatrical reaction as he went to ground. There was an expectation that VAR might intervene, but after a short review the incident, the official’s on-field decision was allowed to stand.

The award subsequently left onlookers and television pundits questioning whether there had been enough contact to justify the referee’s decision, with Chris Sutton stating in commentary “Penrice has played Nick Walsh like a piccolo.” While Rangers will argue that Penrice was impeded, St Mirren were left feeling aggrieved by a call that had a significant bearing on the contest.

The controversy provided Saints with a legitimate grievance and raised questions about the threshold for awarding penalties, particularly when VAR elects not to overturn the referee's original judgement. One that is sure to divide opinion...

Ryan Naderi has emerged as an increasingly influential figure during a period in which injuries to Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland have left Rangers short of attacking options. The forward has responded admirably, combining his physical presence and willingness to lead the line with an impressive goalscoring return. His six goals and three assists in his previous eight league appearances underline the extent of his recent contribution.

Against St Mirren, he provided further evidence of the growing importance he is assuming under McInnes by putting the disappointment of an early miss quickly behind him to break the deadlock from the penalty spot after 18 minutes. The German was coolness personified in his stuttered run-up before sending he goalkeeper the wrong way. Amid a hectic run of fixtures, his ability to deliver consistently is proving invaluable.

Beyond the numbers, it is Naderi's all-round game that appears to have particularly caught his manager’s eye. McInnes was effusive in his praise of the striker's physicality, work-rate and ability to stretch opposition defences post-match. His willingness to run the channels, attack space and bring others into play offers Rangers another dimension in the final third.

McInnes also revealed that Naderi has been practising penalties regularly in training, with that additional work translating into greater assurance when stepping up under pressure. Having inherited a squad without an established penalty specialist or set-piece take following James Tavernier’s exit, the Rangers boss will be pleased to have identified a player increasingly comfortable taking responsibility in decisive moments. Naderi's conversion was another demonstration of that growing confidence.

Naderi has certainly taken his opportunity to impress and strengthened his claim for a regular starting position. There is still room for improvement, but his relentless energy makes him an increasingly difficult player for McInnes to overlook. The question now is whether he can maintain those level when Rangers' attacking options return to full fitness. For the time being, he is making a compelling case to be one of the first names on the team sheet.

#1863. Man Utd suffer blow as Michael Carrick reveals how long Carlos Baleba is out for

Manchester United Carlos Baleba is not expected to return until December at the earliest after suffering a hamstring injury.

The summer signing was forced off early in the second-half of Tuesday’s Champions League game against Roma.

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to pull the trigger on goal.

Baleba appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch. Having already missed the opening five games of the campaign as a result of an ankle injury he suffered during pre-season with Brighton, he now faces another spell on the sidelines.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Providing an update in his pre-match press conference ahead of the visit of Aston Villa on Sunday, Carrick confirmed Baleba will be sidelined for the duration of the international break which begins after this weekend’s fixtures.

‘We don’t know exactly, but it’ll be a number of weeks,” Carrick said when asked about the severity of Baleba’s injury.

‘It’s definitely not this week and it won’t be any time over the international break. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.’

#1861. Rangers away-day concerns give way to renewed optimism as Dan Neil outlines blueprint for silverware

There was something reassuringly uncomplicated about Rangers' 2-0 victory over St Mirren. After a sequence of performances in which attacking promise had not always been matched by defensive security or an ability to put opponents away, this was a night when they got the fundamentals right and the points secured without undue drama.

In Dan Neil’s case, it served as a reminder that Rangers’ away form need not be a source of anxiety. They head into the international break in high spirits and safe in the knowledge that they are within touching distance of Premiership leaders Celtic.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Rangers' recent away performances had exposed a gap between their form at Ibrox and their consistency on the road. Goal scorer Neil acknowledged that concern, describing the win in Paisley as an important response to two disappointing results on their travels in recent weeks.

“It was a good result going into the break,” the stand-in captain admitted. “It was really important that we got that and got back to keeping clean sheets. One of the big things we spoke about before the game, other than clean sheets, is coming away from home and putting in a good performance. The last two away results and performances really haven't been us. We didn’t want it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

“Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. The better our away form is, the better chance we're going to stand [of winning the title]. Every good team just finds a way to win. Obviously we'd like to win by four or five goals every week, but unfortunately that's just not football. I do think it's an area that we can improve on, though.

“These are potential banana skin games. It's important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you've seen that. Our home form speaks for itself, but like I said, the last two away results haven't been great for us. So it was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us.”

The international break provides Rangers with an opportunity to recover ahead of a gruelling winter schedule, although Neil acknowledged that the interruption could also disrupt their rhythm.

”There's definitely pros and cons to international breaks,” he stated. “It's a chance to recharge your batteries a little bit after an intense run of games. But it also kind of halts your momentum a little bit. I think it's important that you take the positives out of the break.

“We can rest and recover ahead of the tough winter months. Hopefully all the boys come back unscathed and have good games with their international teams. I’ll be working hard at the training ground as well as having a few days off and we'll come back ready to fire again.”

There is also a shot at silverware on the horizon. Rangers have five fixtures to negotiate before their Premier Sports Cup final appearance, and Neil is conscious that momentum must be maintained.

“I'm sure we'll relay that message when all the boys are back together,” Neil added. “It's a great chance for us to build some momentum again after a break, going into that final. It's important that we take each test in isolation and not look too far ahead. When the final comes round, it comes round. We've got five really important fixtures before that in which we need to pick up as many points as we can.”

#1859. Saturday's Bundesliga predictions including Mainz vs. Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund vs. Elversberg

By Carter White | 07 Nov 2026 00:05, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 00:05

Today's Bundesliga predictions include Bayern Munich's trip to Mainz 05 and Borussia Dortmund's hosting of recently-promoted Elversberg.

Borussia Dortmund must maintain the pace at the top of the Bundesliga on Saturday, when they welcome Elversberg to Signal Iduna Park.

Black and Yellow are second in the table with 18 points and currently trail Bayern Munich due to goal difference, while newly-promoted Elversberg are in seventh place with 13 points.

Elversberg will almost certainly prove to be challenging opponents given their impressive display last time out.

However, their record away from home is far from perfect, while BVB have been excellent at home, so perhaps Dortmund will be able to keep the pressure on Bayern.

>Borussia Dortmund vs. Elversberg preview

Bayern Munich will hope to maintain their place at the top of the Bundesliga by beating hosts Mainz 05 on Saturday at Mewa Arena.

The Bavarians' tally of 18 points is the same as second-placed Borussia Dortmund, whose inferior goal difference keeps them behind heading into matchweek nine, whereas Mainz are ninth with 10 points.

Bayern may have several injury issues to contend with, but Mainz have struggled considerably in recent weeks.

The visitors could enjoy a fruitful afternoon at Mewa Arena, and striker Kane will relish to opportunity to add to his tally.

Hoping to distance themselves from the Bundesliga's relegation zone, SC Paderborn will welcome European hopefuls Eintracht Frankfurt to Home Deluxe Arena on Saturday.

The hosts are searching for their second win in six games, while Die Adler could earn a third on the bounce.

Paderborn have struggled to score this season, but given their commendable record at the back, they are unlikely to suffer a thrashing this weekend.

Frankfurt will be buoyed by their improved results in recent weeks, though they will need to defy their form on the road to secure all three points, so expect to see a close-fought game.

>Paderborn vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview

Desperate to end their Bundesliga slump, Augsburg will travel to face RB Leipzig at Red Bull Arena on Saturday.

Die Roten Bullen are hoping to bounce back from their midweek defeat, with Die Fuggerstadter winless in six league games.

Leipzig may have been beaten by Man City in midweek, but their record at Red Bull Arena speaks for itself, and they should be able to get the better of their struggling opponents on Saturday.

Augsburg will be desperate for a win this weekend, yet they arrive as significant underdogs against a team that have not conceded on home turf in the league.

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga comes from the MHPArena as Stuttgart welcome a high-flying Werder Bremen side.

While the hosts look to bounce back from a disappointing Champions League defeat, the visitors will have their sights set on extending their unbeaten league run to eight games.

Werder Bremen might have serious momentum under their wings, but their away form is a concern ahead of the trip to Stuttgart.

Two of the previous eight meetings between these sides have ended in 2-2 draws, and another stalemate would not be particularly surprising, especially given both teams' recent goalscoring form in the Bundesliga.

#1858. Barnsley FC boss Daniel Stendel explains Patrick Kelly call and salutes Cameron McGeehan after FA Cup rout

Barnsley head coach Daniel Stendel saluted Cameron McGeehan after the midfielder’s FA Cup hat-trick against Aldershot Town.

The Reds are struggling near the foot of the League One table but put on an attacking clinic against the fifth-tier Shots, advancing into the second round with a 7-2 victory.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McGeehan stole the show with a hat-trick and Stendel felt the 31-year-old was deserving of his treble.

He said: “I'm really pleased for him. I think he deserves it. He works a lot and he keeps his head up every time and tries to push the team.

“He pushes himself every day, in every training session. Also around the team, he tries to push everybody. I'm really happy for him that he scored three goals.

“We deserved, after this long time, a win, especially at home. And I'm happy that we scored seven goals. It's also good for the confidence.

“I know it's a National League team, but it doesn't matter. You have to play like we played today. And we really focused a long time in the game, and we scored some really good goals. I'm happy for the boys, for the result, and also for the supporters there in the stadium today.”

Barnsley conceded twice in the final 15 minutes - but Stendel made a point of focusing solely on the positive aspects of the afternoon.

He said: “I say to me (myself), after the game, I keep only the positive things.”

Stendel named a strong starting XI but there was no place for influential midfielder Patrick Kelly, who only featured as a substitute.

Barnsley’s boss has revealed the decision was made with Kelly’s fitness in mind, with the 22-year-old having struggled with an injury of late.

Stendel explained: “He had, in the last three weeks after the Stockport game, some problems, and he tried to train sometimes with painkillers.

“We gave him a bit of time at the start of the week to recover, especially because next week he's going to play the international games with Northern Ireland.

“Then we decided to start with Daniel Johnson for the first time today, and I think it was the right decision for him, and also a chance for DJ to get more game time, especially when we look forward to next week.”

It was fitting reward for a Lions team who had the better chances, and were finishing normal time the stronger too against full-time Conference side Sutton.

Befitting their status two divisions above Guiseley, it was Sutton who started the stronger, without making it count for anything.

In the fifth minute Ollie Brown was caught under a long ball but when Jermaine Francis played the ball across, Joe Knight was unable to stretch onto it.

The pair almost combined the other way around a few minutes later, Knight playing a nice ball down the channel, but Jack Hall was quick off his line to deny Francis.

Emmanule Osadebe volleyed wide, as did Knight after a break down Sutton's left.

Middlesbrough product Sam Folarin spooned a good chance when Guiseley failed to deal with a long ball.

But once the Lions got to grips with the game, they created the better first-half chances but most fell to defenders.

Elliot Owen headed wide at a 27th-minute corner and two minutes later a great chance fell to left-back Brown arriving at the back post but putting the ball beyond the near.

Form Harrogate Town promotion winner Jack Emmett volleyed off target when the ball came loose to him, and Brown had a goalbound header nodded away after Cam Wilson's free-kick caused problems.

Right-back Lucas Odunston volleyed into a crowd of defenders after Sutton goalkeeper Brits' clearance was cut out.

Half-time was stretched out to 36 minutes by a medical incident, and the second half started in much less open fashion.

But Guiseley winger Amir Berchil got stronger as the game wnt on.

Harrison Hoppr released him with an excellent ball in the 53rd minute but when the ball came over, Murphy's shot was blocked.

When a Wilson free-kick was headed behind for a corner, it was played to Hoppr for a blocked shot.

Jake Taylor headed wide after Tinker did well to snuff out a dangerous break down Sutton's lft.

But it was in the final 10 minutes that the Lions came on strong.

When Berchil did well to beat Besart Topallaj, Murphy fell at the vital minute, the pristine playing surface becoming slipper under the floodlights and the cold night air.

The home fans were celebrating an 86th-minute penalty, only for the referee to rule Tinker was brought down just outside the area. Thewlis made a hash of the free-kick, but that would soon be forgotten.

Berchil got on the end of a long ball as the game ticked into stoppage time, but after cutting inside, could only shoot at the goalkeeper.

That was what Omar Mussa did a couple of minutes late for Sutton's first shot on target of the match.

As minds started to turn to extra-time, Thewlis had other ideas, forcing his way into the Sutton ara and winning the spot kick which would tchd his name into Guiseley history.

Guiseley: Hall; Odunston, Owen, Mbeka, Brown (Thewlis 78); Hopper, Staniland; Wilson (White 78), Emmett (Tinker 57), Berchil (Iggulden 90+6); Murphy.

Unused substitutes: Roxburgh, Lund, Longbottom, Wadsworth, Sinfield.

Sutton United: Brits; Urpens (Nightingale HT), Kirk, Topalloj, Brookes; Osadebe (Mussa 78), Taylor; Folarin, Knight (Babalola 65), Francis (Ogbonna 65); Carter.

Unused substitutes: Bell, Haigh, Moore-Taylor, Njoku, Amartey.

#1852. Amorim offers honest Milan reflection: “We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team”

Ruben Amorim continued the criticism of his AC Milan side after their dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, branding them ‘not ready’ to compete on multiple fronts.

Amorim made the decision to enact six changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Inter convincingly in the derby at the weekend, but it backfired as his team never got going last night and were well-beaten by the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is reported that after the game the Portuguese coach gave a long speech to his players about their attitude and effort levels. Milan remain incredibly inconsistent on this front, as they continue to alternate very encouraging performances with disastrous and listless ones.

Amorim laid into his team during an interview with Sky after the final whistle, and then he spoke to the CBS Sports Golazo studio shortly afterwards. The exchange was transcribed by MilanNews.

Yesterday you were talking about identity, about character. Was this the difference?

“Yes, technically, tactically, and above all mentally, they were superior and deserved to win. Today we weren’t ready to play professional football, and I felt it. We need to look within ourselves and do better.”

And in the Champions League the level would be even higher…

“We have to focus on the small details, without thinking about the Champions League or anything like that. We just have to focus on improving the more specific aspects of football: the mentality, the heart, the passion. We have to improve on that.”

What is Ferencvaros’ level in European football, how do you rate them?

“I don’t know, it depends on the opponent, but they’re doing very well. They have four wins in four games, a clear identity, and today they were superior to us.”

What did this match tell you about Milan?

“That we’re not ready. We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team. We have moments, in some games, where we’re really strong, but then we can’t maintain our level, especially mentally. So this game told me and all of us that we’re not ready to be a very strong team.”

During the first half, I noticed you were very energetic on the sidelines, and then it almost seemed like you stopped giving directions. Can you tell there’s a certain lack of understanding within the team and that they’re not playing the way you’d like?

“No, I just do what I feel at the time, and sometimes I don’t do certain things just for show. We didn’t play well, that’s for sure; we had a completely different attitude in the last league game, while today we weren’t mentally prepared to fight for the win, and that’s what we need to work on.”

If there hadn’t been the derby at the weekend, do you think this match would have gone better?

“I have no idea, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter, we have to be ready to play every three days in different competitions. So it doesn’t matter if we had a match before or not. I think we have to improve a lot in all aspects of the game.”

Torriani played his first match as a starter. How do you rate his performance today?

“I think he did well in the first half. He had a difficult time with a pass, but Lorenzo doesn’t bear any responsibility for the team’s performance. In fact, in the first half he gave us time to try to make some changes in the second half. So Lorenzo just has to keep working. We have to improve as a team to be stronger.”

#1850. Saturday's Ligue 1 predictions including Paris Saint-Germain vs. Troyes

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 00:10, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 21:12

Today's Ligue 1 predictions include Paris Saint-Germain's home meeting with Troyes in their final outing before the international break.

Ten places separate Auxerre and Paris FC in the Ligue 1 table ahead of Saturday's matchday 10 fixture at Stade de l'Abbe-Deschamps.

Liam Rosenior's men could theoretically finish the weekend joint-top if they secure maximum points against the side with the division's worst defensive record and Paris Saint-Germain lose to Troyes.

Auxerre's league-worst defensive record is concerning, but conceding just five goals across four home matches suggests that Saturday's assignment may be less straightforward than the table implies.

Paris have struggled to replicate their home performances on the road, and Sinayoko's potential absence could leave Rosenior's men settling for a point.

Paris Saint-Germain enter Saturday's gameweek 10 Ligue 1 encounter at Parc des Princes seeking a seventh consecutive league victory and an 11th straight win across all competitions.

The European champions have not dropped points in two months, and Luis Enrique's men are heavy favourites to extend their dominant run against Troyes, who have claimed just one victory in their last seven matches.

Troyes have restored some confidence with four points and consecutive clean sheets, but containing the European champions represents a considerably greater challenge than their recent assignments.

Fresh from putting six past Villarreal, PSG have enough match-winners to overcome their injury absences and extend their winning sequence with a comfortable home victory.

#1849. JJ Gabriel reveals key motivation behind Real Madrid transfer after Man Utd exit

JJ Gabriel has revealed the key motivation behind his impending move to Real Madrid after turning his back on Manchester United.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, informed United of his desire to leave in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, but has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

The forward joined United’s academy four years ago and quickly established himself as one of the most highly-rated youngsters at the club, featuring for the U18 side at the age of just 14.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Gabriel played under Michael Carrick during the club’s pre-season camp, but his entourage are understood to have grown unhappy with his first-team integration and playing opportunities at United.

The teenager, who has an Irish passport, could finalise a move to the Spanish giants as early as January next year, with United reportedly set to receive £350,000 in compensation.

And in a brief interview with the Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel revealed he has one particular goal in mind for his time at Real.

‘My dream is to win a Ballon d’Or,’ he said.

When asked about a potential move to Barcelona instead, Gabriel simply responded: ‘Obviously, Madrid.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

A move to Real is a bold step at such a young age, and United legend Ryan Giggs believes Gabriel may have been better served following the example of Max Dowman, whose development is not being rushed by Arsenal or Mikel Arteta.

📰🔜 JJ Gabriel with Marca’s front page confirming the move to Real Madrid is close: “Can I keep this [newspaper] with me?”. pic.twitter.com/cerdxXsbE4

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient.

‘If you’re on the right trajectory then just bide your time, no matter how good you are.

‘Max Dowman is unbelievable but he’s not playing for Arsenal at the moment.

‘I’m sure he’ll bide his time, I’m sure he’s getting impatient, but he’s not kicking off, he knows in a couple of years time he might be the main man for Arsenal.’

#1848. Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder rues 'missed opportunity' after defeat to Charlton Athletic

Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder was left to rue a “missed opportunity” after his side were beaten 2-1 by Charlton Athletic.

The Blades had a chance to move into the Championship play-off places at The Valley but left the capital empty-handed.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Millenic Alli fired the hosts ahead after 12 minutes and Matty Godden restored the Charlton lead after Jordan Ayew’s equaliser.

Wilder said: “You look at the results after we came in and you scratch your head. But the one we have to concentrate on is our own and we have not done enough things right.

“We didn’t capitalise on our moments to get the result we were all after. I’m not going to take a wrecking ball to it.

“There is always emotion in it – when you win then you’re going up and when you don’t then it is a different narrative.

“We will keep calm, like I have all the way through. I kept calm after we beat Wrexham, Bristol City and when we won on Tuesday. There are mini setbacks, mini highs and mini lows that we need to deal with.

“It is a missed opportunity. I’d have loved to have climbed into the top seven, but we need to rest and recover over the international break.”

Wilder was particularly frustrated by the nature of Charlton’s goals, as he felt the Addicks did not have to work “unbelievably hard” to register them.

He said: “It’s been a frustrating day. They have not had to work unbelievably hard for their goals.

“We have to be stronger in the lead up to the first one. Michael [Cooper] has been outstanding and it is a difficult one because it has dipped and bounced in front of him.

“The second one is the frustrating one. I played at full-back and there are going to be times that wingers go past you.

“The distances between Liam Kitching, Mark McGuinness and Japh [Tanganga] were too big. Godden is a goal-scorer and they allow him to get in front. It gave them a huge boost and huge energy.”

Charlton boss Nathan Jones, meanwhile, said: “Relief is a big thing – emotionally – because of everything that has gone on. That was more like us from start to finish. We were front-footed and had real control in our play.

“I’m really proud of the group, because they’ve had to cope with so much noise and pressure.

“We have lost five or six people this week through injury and what not. So to respond in the manner we did, apart from Wembley it is probably my favourite result at this football club.

“It was wonderful. It’s only one win, but it’s an important one. We won’t over-egg it because it is just one win.

“The crowd have been really good with me. I probably used up all their patience in midweek. Hopefully I’ve taken one step back into credit.”

“Overall I’m very happy with how we’ve started the season – 14 games in, I’m happy with how brave we’ve been and how many points we have got.

‘They spend money on forwards, they spend money on midfield players like you’ve never seen and yet they still haven’t got a defence,’ Warnock told The Mirror.

‘I don’t understand how a top club like that can’t buy defenders – and they’ve never had any full backs that can defend either.

#1841. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi makes Pedro Porro selection admission ahead of Leeds clash

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 00:15, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 00:15

Tottenham Hotspur boss Roberto De Zerbi has admitted he has "not decided" whether Pedro Porro will start Saturday's Premier League clash with Leeds United at Elland Road.

Spurs will carry significant momentum into the lunchtime fixture after recording three consecutive victories, including a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace last weekend.

Pedro Porro featured as a half-time substitute against the Eagles, his second consecutive appearance off the bench after returning from a hamstring injury.

Speaking after the match, De Zerbi revealed that it was Porro who made the decision not to start against Palace.

"Pedro is ready, we didn't take risks," De Zerbi said. "Speaking with him, he decided before the game and he was very honest with me."

While Porro is believed to have no physical issues, last weekend's season casts some doubt as to whether he will start at Elland Road on Saturday.

De Zerbi refused to confirm whether the Spain international will feature in his lineup when he spoke to reporters on Friday.

“I have not decided yet about Pedro Porro, but it is not a tactical decision,” De Zerbi said.

“When Pedro Porro is fit, he plays because he is a top player, top guy, leader, clear leader, without problems.”

While Porro has struggled with injury this time, Spurs will be keen for Porro to start Saturday's fixture, especially as he has been deemed fit enough to make the latest Spain squad.

However, if he is not ready to start on Sunday, the versatile Archie Gray would retain his place for a fifth consecutive Premier League start

The 20-year-old scored in the 2-0 win over Palace before he made way for Porro at the break amid fears he could receive a second yellow card after being cautioned in the 15th minute.

If he does feature at Elland Road, it would be his first appearance against Leeds since leaving the club for Tottenham in 2024.

#1840. Steven Gerrard makes Michael Carrick sack claim ahead of Man Utd vs Aston Villa

Steven Gerrard believes it could be ‘tough’ to envisage Michael Carrick surviving the international break if Manchester United lose to Aston Villa on Sunday.

United ended their nine-match winless run in midweek after a superb comeback win against Roma in the Champions League.

But the pressure remains firmly on Carrick’s shoulders heading into the weekend, with the Red Devils sitting 17th in the Premier League and without a win in the competition since late August.

Unai Emery’s Villa side will look to pile the pressure back on United with a victory at Old Trafford, and Gerrard fears a United defeat may make it hard for Carrick to return as manager after the international break.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘Sometimes a performance against a certain opposition in a certain way can give the board a little bit more belief a little bit more hope,’ Gerrard said on TNT Sports.

‘Michael is having a tough time, and I think the next league game is crucial. I think if he can get that win, I think everyone will think this might be the few stepping stones for them to get into better form.

‘But everyone knows what a defeat [in] the last game before an international break could do. If you lose that on the back of not winning a nine in the league, I think it could be tough for him.’

Speculation over Carrick’s potential replacement has been rife in recent weeks, with Unai Emery, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann all said to be under consideration.

But Gerrard believes that Carrick is far from the ‘biggest problem’ at Old Trafford, as he blamed the club’s players and board for letting down a swathe of recent managerial appointments.

#1838. Crawley Town to celebrate 130th anniversary with special edition shirt for Newport County game

To kick off the week, supporters will have the chance to purchase 1 of only 130 limited-edition shirts. The shirts will come in a commemorative box, along with a special 130th key ring and pin badge set, an anniversary scarf and commemorative certificate of authenticity. The shirt will be revealed on the morning of Monday, the 7th and will be released on sale shortly after, both in-store and online.

Each fan-edition shirt will have an embedded commemorative patch, making each shirt unique, as they will all have a different edition number between 1-130. More details on the sale process will be released in due course.

Following specialised social media coverage on Tuesday, the club will then celebrate the anniversary with an evening in the Innovation Group Executive Suite on Wednesday, December 9.

Tickets for the event will cost £30pp and include an inside look at the workings of the Broadfield Stadium, a curry meal service including poppadoms and sundries, and a look around a specially curated exhibition that captures parts of the club’s rich history. After the food service, the club will host a series of interview panels with former and current players from different eras, giving them a chance to tell their stories and chat about the best moments from their time at the club. More former players will be in attendance as the club’s guests of honour, and will be hosted in hospitality for the match before being paraded to fans at half-time. #1836. Guiseley manager Ian Richards on FA Cup shock – we deserved it

The Lions reached the second round of the FA Cup in dramatic fashion, but there was nothing fortunate about their 1-0 win over Sutton United.

The only goal of the game was a Jordan Thewlis penalty in the fourth added minute, but a home win was a fair reflection of how Guiseley outperformed a team two divisions above them in the Conference.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I think the performance deserved the result," commented manager Richards.

"I know we scored in the closing minutes with a penalty but their first shot on target came from 25 yards in the 92nd minute. I thought we had some excellent chances. We had a couple of penalty shouts prior to that one.

"We had excellent chances in the first and second half where we could have won the game.

"What I was really pleased with against a top National League side who played the strongest team, changed the personnel (during the game), changed the shape of the side that kept a clean sheet.

"Again we called on sub to continue that momentum, so another squad effort and the club's really proud of them.

"They've created history, they've created memories and they've created even more connections with the supporters and people within the club.

"They're a really honest group and I'm so pleased for them.

"For me the cups are for the fans, the club and the players to have those memories.

"Obviously as a manager my priority will always be the league and I've got to think about that very soon. But for the players and the club we need to enjoy these memories.

"It's a short career as a player but it's the third time this club has got to the second round of the FA Cup so we need to mark and celebrate the history that's been made.

"I thought the last 10 minutes we've been so much stronger.

"They really struggled with the pace and the energy that we're playing with. Our identity came through and that's what wins the penalty.

"It was a bit like when we were schoolboys. He's won it, he takes it. Cam Wilson's our penalty-taker but Jordan's good from the penalty spot.

"I was very calm. Even when the (unused) players ran on and celebrated. I was very calm there."

And on top of the win which puts Northern Premier League Guiseley in Monday's second round draw – the lowest-ranked side whose place was confirmed on Saturday - there was another element which delighted Richards.

"The one thing I've been disappointed in is the brilliant run we've had is the last five games we've conceded goals, maybe soft goals or preventable goals," he said.

"Clean sheets win you promotions, win you big cup games like this. We kept a clean sheet. We always know that from front players and attacking players as well, we're going to score at some point."

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

#1831. 'It really hurts' - Doncaster Rovers boss Grant McCann addresses sack chants after shock FA Cup exit

Doncaster Rovers manager Grant McCann conceded it “hurt” to hear the club’s supporters chanting about him being sacked in the morning.

Sections of the fanbase made their anger known as Doncaster crashed out of the FA Cup against fifth-tier Kidderminster Harriers. The hosts were 2-0 by half-time courtesy of goals from Lewis Walker and Maz Kouhyar and David Davis extended the lead after the interval.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The humiliating loss followed a 6-1 league mauling at the hands of Milton Keynes Dons and significantly ramped up the pressure on McCann and his underperforming players.

As reported by the Doncaster Free Press, McCann said: “It really hurts. When fans are singing ‘you’re getting sacked in the morning’ and that the players aren’t fit to wear the shirt...

“I've brought every single one of the to the club, so that's another indictment on me. The boys are really stinging in there. They’re hurt.”

Not only are Doncaster are now out of the FA Cup, they are languishing in 20th in the League One table after seven defeats across their opening 13 games.

McCann said: “What I do know in football is that you've got two choices. You throw it all up in the air or you do it and carry on, or you stick together. You get through the dark times.

“At this moment in time, it's a tough period. It's a really tough period. We're not performing well enough. We're not doing the basics of football well enough.”

“The fans are entitled to their opinions. All we can do is make sure that we are united as a group. There's a real siege mentality in there. We stick together, like we always do.”

#1830. Jamie Redknapp names Arsenal’s biggest title rivals after Man City defeat

Jamie Redknapp believes Arsenal will ‘run away’ with the Premier League title this season and has named Brighton as their nearest challengers.

Arsenal moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League with a 1-0 win at home to Hull City.

Manchester City then suffered their third straight defeat in the Premier League as they were beaten 3-1 by Nottingham Forest on Saturday evening.

Brighton will overtake City and move into second if they beat Brentford on Sunday and Redknapp admits he is struggling to see a credible threat to Arsenal this season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘They [Man City] obviously miss Semenyo, he’s a big player for them in the wide areas but they’ve still got people in wide positions who can cause problems,’ Redknapp told Sky Sports.

‘That one today is a sore one, it gives you the feeling right now in terms of who can challenge Arsenal? I just don’t see one.

‘If you look at the league table, I think right now, probably the one you’d point to, and I never thought I’d say this at the start of the year, but it’s Brighton.

‘Arsenal have got Saliba coming back, the players they’ve got defensively, you’d never see Arsenal look as open as we saw Manchester City look [against Forest].

‘I don’t really see anything else other than Arsenal running away with this title at the moment.

#1827. Arsenal learn William Saliba France decision as Zinedine Zidane names squad

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 00:49, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 02:33

Arsenal defender William Saliba has not been selected in Zinedine Zidane's latest France squad.

Saliba has not played any competitive football since he was forced off in France's World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain due to a back issue.

The 25-year-old's injury struggles opened the door for summer signing Ezri Konsa to form a strong central defensive partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes that has helped Arsenal move three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

However, Mikel Arteta will soon have a big selection decision to make, with Saliba back in training and on the verge of making his long-awaited return.

Saliba was named as a substitute for Wednesday's 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League and should be in the matchday squad for Saturday's Premier League meeting with Hull City.

With Saliba available for selection, Arteta revealed that Arsenal had been in "close contact' with France ahead of their squad announcement.

Speaking in Friday's pre-match press conference, Arteta said: "We've been in very close contact. I think they are announcing their squad at 5pm this evening.

"They have all the information. Now it's about them, about Zinedine in this case to make the call. We will accept whatever it is.

"I think it's something between them. Willy needs minutes as well. I know how much he loves to be in the national team.

"It's a new manager, a really exciting one as well, so whatever he has decided is fine for us."

??? La liste de Zinédine Zidane pour nos 2 derniers matchs de la phase de groupes de Ligue des Nations, face à l’Italie et à la Turquie ! Première convocation pour Pablo Pagis ? https://t.co/Tmwmhcgg8C

While Saliba could benefit from some competitive minutes, Arsenal will surely welcome the news that the 25-year-old has been left out of Zidane's squad.

Zidane has seemingly exercised caution with Saliba's return to action, which means the 25-year-old will not play under the France boss until at least March next year.

Instead of picking Saliba, Zidane has named Manchester United's Leny Yoro and Liverpool's Jeremy Jacquet among his centre-back options.

Dayot Upamecano, Ibrahima Konate and Pierre Kalulu have also been called up for the final international window of 2026.

#1826. Paul Merson says Arsenal star has been ‘like a new signing’ after Hull win

Paul Merson reserved special praise for Martin Odegaard following Arsenal’s gritty 1-0 victory over Hull City, claiming the midfielder has been ‘like a new signing’ this season.

Arsenal had looked on course to drop points for only the second time this term as newly promoted Hull dug in and managed to frustrate their hosts, with Declan Rice coming close to breaking the deadlock on three occasions.

Noni Madueke also had his head in his hands after being denied by Konstantinos Tzolakis with the minutes ticking down in front of an increasingly agitated Emirates crowd.

But the pressure told with 18 minutes remaining of normal time as Tzolakis again kept out Madueke, only for Odegaard to pounce and poke the ball home on the rebound to cue rapturous scenes in north London.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The reigning Premier League champions preserved their narrow advantage to ensure they moved six points clear at the top of the table after Manchester City were stunned in a 3-1 defeat away to Nottingham Forest.

High-flying Brighton – the only team to get the better of Arsenal – will look to close the gap to five points when they play host to Brentford later this afternoon.

‘You know Hull are going to sit ten behind the ball and make it very difficult,’ ex-Arsenal and England midfielder Merson said of Arsenal’s win over Hull on Sky Sports.

‘If you score early, you just go on and then win 3-0 or 4-0 and it would be a nice day at the office. That didn’t happen.

‘Hull defended very well and it took Martin Odegaard to break them down if I’m being honest.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Noni Madueke comes inside, hits a shot, it gets parried… he’s the first one to react and there’s two defenders in front of him, about four or five yards in front of him, but because of his reaction, he runs past them, he hits it, there’s a slight deflection and it goes underneath the goalkeeper’s arms.’

Merson felt Hull shot-stopper Tzolakis was the man of the match in a game which could later be seen as vital if Arsenal are to successfully defend their title this season.

He added: ‘Arsenal weren’t great but they won and this could be one of those games you look back on at the end of the season and go, “Remember the Hull game when we nicked it at the end”, but yeah, Hull will come away and think they did alright.

‘For me, the goalkeeper was the man of the match for Hull so that tells you everything. Arsenal weren’t great but it was a great result.’

Odegaard was once again the heartbeat of everything Arsenal did well to continue what has been an outstanding start to the 2026/27 campaign for the Gunners captain.

The crucial 72nd-minute strike took the Norwegian’s goalscoring tally to five in all competitions this season. He managed only one goal in 36 appearances last term.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard.

‘He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’

Arsenal will hope to tighten their vicelike grip on top spot when they return to Premier League action against Newcastle at St James’ Park in a week’s time.

A tough Champions League clash at home to Borussia Dortmund awaits three days later, before Mikel Arteta’s men head back to the Emirates to face off against Manchester City in the English top flight.

#1825. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

Chelsea Sharman-Lowe, Palestra, Colwill (Acheampong, 80), Palmer (Kellyman, 80), Gittens (Tosin), Essugo (Walsh, 80), Pedro (Delap, 80), Hato (Anselmino, 62), Fofana (Sarr, 80), Estêvão (Satpayev, 70), Lavia (Nicoll-Jazuli, 46).Substitutes not used Watson, Curd, Subuloye, Emenalo, Kavuma-McQueen.Goal Estêvão (21).Tottenham Hotspur Kinsky, Robertson (Kyerematen, 72; Tingey, 90+1), Davies (Takai, 81), Van Hecke (Danso, 46), Gray, Gallagher (Hardy, 54), Tonali (Donley, 81), Bergvall (Hall, 72), Tel (Williams-Barnett, 76), Solanke (Richarlison, 46), Solomon (Moore, 67).Substitutes not used Dubravka, Scarlett, Russell-Denny, Melia, Yang, Ajayi, Byrne, Tye Hall.Booked Gallagher (10).Goals Tonali (17), Richarlison.Sent off Danso (49).

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign begins at Brentford on August 22.

July 28- Western Sydney Wanderers 4 Chelsea 6Today- Chelsea 1 Tottenham 2August 5- Chelsea vs JuventusAugust 8- Chelsea vs AC MilanAugust 9- Johor Darul Ta’z vs ChelseaAugust 15- Chelsea vs Real Sociedad

Chelsea begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham on August 24.

Possession: Chelsea 46%-54% TottenhamShots: 14-7Shots on target: 4-4Corners: 1-1

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

Danny Murphy says Arsenal’s title challengers should be very ‘worried’ that the champions find themselves six points clear at the top despite not ‘really playing that well’ for much of the season.

Arsenal increased their imperious lead at the summit thanks to a hard-fought 1-0 victory at home to Hull on Saturday, in which Martin Odegaard scored the only goal of the game to continue his outstanding start to the campaign.

At the City Ground, meanwhile, Manchester City were stunned by a Liam Delap-inspired Nottingham Forest to fall further behind the Gunners in what was their third successive defeat in the Premier League.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

#1821. Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with familiar problem after Hull win

Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with an old problem that became so cliched that it was featured in a sit-com 18 years ago.

The Gunners beat Hull City 1-0 on Saturday in the Premier League, with Martin Odegaard scoring the only goal at the Emirates.

Any problem Arsenal are struggling with is not too serious as that win, followed by Manchester City’s defeat at Nottingham Forest, put Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the table.

However, Arteta was frustrated with Arsenal only scoring one goal and it not coming until the 72nd minute, despite dominating possession and producing 21 shots at goal.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Sometimes the inability to even produce a shot was the problem, despite having the ball in dangerous areas plenty of times.

In a 2008 episode of The IT Crowd, Moss and Roy both try to ingratiate with football fans by learning the phrase: ‘The thing about Arsenal is they’re always trying to walk it in.’

Arteta seems to have a similar take on his team, accusing them of trying to score the ‘perfect goal’ against defensively-minded teams.

‘[We need to] be more efficient,’ the Arsenal manager said. ‘We are one against one against the keeper. That’s happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing.

‘So many shots that have been deflected, blocked. We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that’s it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that’s going to change the course of the game.

‘We had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that. And then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box, insisting, insisting and insisting until we are able to break them down. And this is exactly how we won the game.’

Odegaard is Arsenal’s top-scorer this season with five goals in all competitions and three in the Premier League.

While Arsenal’s attack does not always penetrate as much as Arteta would like, the defence is incredibly reliable.

Another clean sheet meant the Gunners have conceded just five goals in 10 league games and have not conceded in 10 of their 17 matches across all competitions.

Centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes said: ‘If we don’t concede goals, we have a big chance to win games. We are really happy to have another clean sheet.

‘Like I said, when we have a strong team, a strong defence, we don’t concede goals. I think this season, how many is that? Ten clean sheets in the whole competition? This is our standard. We need to keep winning.’

#1820. CM: Amorim let down again in another European debacle – the players whose stock has dropped

There are several players that are at risk of slipping down Ruben Amorim’s pecking order with displays like the one against Ferencvaros.

Calciomercato.com write that three clues add up to mean that we can say with certainty that Milan are not aiming to win the Europa League despite being one of the favourites, at least on paper. The defeats against Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros were determined by two factors.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the attitude of the squad’s key players and the inadequacy of several reserves. The dominant Adrien Rabiot, for example, seems to sink when the Europa League anthem is played. The Frenchman – captain on this occasion due to Mike Maignan’s suspension – wasn’t the only culprit, but was certainly the most obvious.

The thing squad assembled last summer by Gerry Cardinale, Amorim and the management features a strong starting eleven that can compete with anyone (as was the case in the derby), but at the same time lacks alternatives.

In several cases, it’s fair to say that the players aren’t up to the task. Filippo Terracciano’s role is emblematic: already rejected by the previous management, he remained with Milan at Amorim’s request.

His season included 45 poorly played minutes against Benfica before being substituted at half-time, a straight red card as a substitute against Salzburg, and a poor performance against Ferencvaros that drew boos from the crowd.

Doubts are also growing over Ardon Jashari, who – after a few performances that were at least adequate – continues to display obvious technical and tactical limitations. The money spent on him (over €30m) is leading many to run out of patience.

The excellent performances against RB Salzburg and Udinese seemed to have reintroduced a courageous and powerful version of Davide Bartesaghi to Milan, but the most recent test saw him revert to the flaws of last season in terms of personality and concentration.

Pervis Estupinan, on the other hand, seems to have completely disappeared from the radar, having remained on the bench for the entire match against Ferencvaros. The two left-backs have a lot of work to do, and this could influence some transfer choices too.

#1819. Tottenham hit with huge Mathys Tel injury blow as Leeds 'escape red card'

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham will be sweating over the fitness of Mathys Tel during the international break after the forward was forced off against Leeds on Saturday.

In a potentially significant injury blow, the French forward was substituted before half-time after a heavy challenge from Jayden Bogle, who landed his studs on the the Spurs man’s left Achilles.

Tel initially tried to continue before signalling to the Spurs bench that he could not play on, and he was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute.

Bogle was not booked by the referee, John Brooks, and while VAR reviewed the challenge, they did not deem it to meet the threshold for serious foul play.

In a feisty opening 45, Bogle escaped a booking, much to the frustration of Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, who remonstrated with fourth official Josh Smith on the touchline.

Mateus Fernandes had earlier been fortunate not to concede a penalty after appearing to clear the ball inside the area with his arm.

Replays of the decision showed the ball hit the top of Fernandes’ arm, which, by the rules of the game, means it is not a penalty.

The Premier League Match Centre released an explanation for both decisions.

“The referee’s call of no penalty to Leeds United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Fernandes did not commit a handball offence.

VAR: “Confirming the on-field decision of play on. The ball strikes the very top of the arm as he is leaning – in the green zone”.

“The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR.

VAR: “I’m confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”.

"No sense at all," said lead commentator Darren Fletcher on TNT Sports regarding the lack of card for the challenge.

"If you are a referee, you have to at least see the yellow card challenge [on the monitor] if [VAR] don't think it's a red."

Steven Gerrard, on co-commentary, added: "We don't like to see anyone get sent off .... but he's got away with one there."

"They've said no red card, this will create debate," former Spurs midfielder Michael Brown said on BBC 5 Live.

"The stud goes into the back of his Achilles, but the one thing I'll say in his defence, his right foot comes round to win the ball but his left foot just plants down.

"I'll give him the benefit of the doubt but it's still a nasty one. The ref should still go and see it on the monitor."

#1818. Leeds United vs. Tottenham: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 01:44

Tottenham Hotspur will travel to face Leeds United at Elland Road on Saturday in their final Premier League game before the November international break.

Spurs are ninth in the Premier League with 12 points, whereas their hosts are 12th with 11 points, and a win for either would significantly ease relegation fears ahead of the busy winter schedule.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 12.30pm UK time on Saturday.

Tottenham will travel to Leeds United's Elland Road, a stadium with a capacity of 37,633.

The Premier League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.55pm and run until midnight

Tottenham have finally found form under Roberto De Zerbi, with the club having won each of their last three league games.

Some fans were concerned about the possibility of relegation at the start of the season, but a win on the weekend could see Spurs rise as high as sixth.

A European charge should be seen as a successful campaign, and it would no doubt be seen as a successful season from Leeds, who could move as high as seventh with an additional three points.

Daniel Farke's main goal will be to avoid demotion yet again, especially as they are only four points ahead of 18th-placed Crystal Palace, and he may even be tempted to accept a draw on Saturday.

Sam Tabuteau rated the Spurs players at Elland Road…

#1815. Why William Saliba is not in Arsenal squad against Hull despite injury return

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba is expected to play for Arsenal’s Under-21s against Aston Villa on Sunday.

The Frenchman has not played a minute this season, with his last competitive appearance coming in July in the World Cup semi-finals.

He has been out with a serious back injury since then, an issue that Arsenal have been extremely cautious with.

However, Saliba has made good progress and recently played 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors friendly.

He was then named in Arsenal’s squad against Slavia Prague on Wednesday night, though he did not come off the bench.

Clubs are able to name more players on the bench in the Champions League than they are in the Premier League and Saliba was not selected in Arsenal’s matchday squad to face Hull on Saturday.

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that was not due to any setback, but rather a plan to get Saliba back up to full fitness.

He is set to be involved when Arsenal’s Under-21s host Villa on Sunday afternoon.

“Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do, to play some minutes on the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”
